logline: A minor god hustling for prayers and a girl whose soul keeps slipping out of her body make an unlikely partnership navigating the border between the living world and the afterlife.

renewal.note: Two seasons aired (2014, 2015). No third season announced as of 2026; the manga by Adachitoka concluded, and Bones has not greenlit further adaptation.

bollymeter.basis: Noragami's first season earns its reputation as solid, all-around entertainment: Bones animates the supernatural action with flair, and the god-shinki mythology gives the show genuine texture. IMDb aggregate sits at 7.8.

seasons.review_body: Noragami's first season aired on MBS from January to March 2014, adapting Adachitoka's manga through Bones. The series blends Shinto mythology, supernatural action, and adolescent longing without overreaching. The three-way dynamic between Yato, a gods-for-hire deity, Hiyori, a girl straddling life and death, and Yukine, a troubled weapon spirit, gives the season genuine emotional stakes. It works as a strong introduction arc, while it also ends before the manga's deeper conflicts fully emerge.

episode_reviews.title: A Housecat, a Stray God, and a Tail
episode_reviews.review_body: Noragami Season 1 Episode 1 'A Housecat, a Stray God, and a Tail' aired January 5, 2014 on MBS as the premiere of Bones' adaptation of Adachitoka's manga. IMDb audiences scored the series 7.8. The premiere establishes Yato as a minor deity advertising his services on bathroom stalls, willing to grant any wish for five yen. The tone is set immediately - comic irreverence over genuine supernatural menace - and Hiyori's accident into the spirit world gives the premise its hook. The three-way dynamic between Yato, Hiyori, and Yukine is established with enough efficiency that the show's Shinto mythology registers as texture rather than exposition. Yato's business card handed out at a crosswalk is the franchise's most economical image of divine underachievement.

episode_reviews.title: To Cut, or Not to Cut
episode_reviews.review_body: Noragami Season 1 Episode 12 'To Cut, or Not to Cut' aired March 23, 2014 on MBS as the season finale of Bones' 12-episode adaptation. IMDb audiences scored the series 7.8. The finale confronts the conflict between Yato and Yukine that had been building since the midpoint - the cost of a weapon spirit's corruption on the god who carries him. The emotional resolution lands harder than the action: a supernatural climax grounded in genuine grief about belonging and purpose. The ritual that forces Yato's hand is the season's moral weight finally made physical, and the episode's closing gesture is more interested in character repair than spectacle. Anime News Network's Aragoto preview later cited the franchise's 'powerful depth of emotion' as the quality Season 2 deepened.

bollymeter.basis: Noragami Aragoto deepens the mythology and raises the emotional stakes considerably over Season 1; Anime News Network's Theron Martin rated it 4.5 out of 5, citing its 'captivating art design and powerful depth of emotion.'

pull_quotes.text: With its captivating art design, lovable characters, and powerful depth of emotion, Noragami Aragoto is bound to be an enjoyable experience.

seasons.review_body: Noragami Aragoto aired from October to December 2015 on MBS, expanding Bishamon's backstory and introducing the god Ebisu across its arcs. The season carries a warmer feel than the first, with art design and emotional depth that better align with the stronger source material. The Bishamon arc in particular explores the poisoned bond between a war god and her unstable shinki, giving the season a tragic weight the earlier season only gestures toward. A mean AniList score of 80 and a focus on emotional resonance position this as the show’s peak.
seasons.season_over_season: Aragoto graduates from promising setup to emotionally complex mythology, with the Bishamon arc delivering the dramatic payoff Season 1 builds toward.

episode_reviews.title: Slay
episode_reviews.review_body: Noragami Season 2 Episode 7 'Slay' aired November 13, 2015 on MBS as the midpoint of Noragami Aragoto's Bishamon arc - the season Anime News Network praised for 'captivating art design and powerful depth of emotion.' IMDb audiences scored the series 7.8. The episode reaches the breaking point of the season's central conflict: the cost of Bishamon's devotion to her troubled shinki, and how a god's refusal to release what is poisoning her has damaged everyone around her. The revelation of what Bishamon has been protecting - and what it has cost her - is rendered with unusual precision for a shonen-adjacent series. Community reviewers consistently identify this as Aragoto's most emotionally loaded single hour, the moment the season's tragic weight becomes impossible to deflect.
